in_hebrew.name: דַּרְבִּי
in_hebrew.meaning: ראש, ראשי, ראשׁ, ראשׁי, ראשׁי, ראשׁי
in_hebrew.long_meaning: דַּרְבִּי (Darbi) - ראש (rosheb) - (the) head, chief, leader, or firstborn. דַּרְבִּי (Darbi) is a title of respect in Hebrew, used to address a teacher, rabbi, or elder. In a Christian context, it may refer to the head or leader of the Church, such as Jesus Christ (Matthew 16:16).

in_greek.name: Δαρβή
in_greek.long_meaning: Δαρβή (Darbē) - ἀρχηγός (archegos) - leader, chief, or head. In the New Testament, Jesus Christ is referred to as the Head of the Church (Colossians 1:18). Δαρβή (Darbē) may also be related to the Greek word ἀρχή (archē) - beginning, origin, or principle, as in the beginning of creation (Genesis 1:1).

in_latin.name: Darbee
in_latin.long_meaning: Darbee - caput (head) - princeps (chief) - primus (first) - magister (teacher or master). In early Christian tradition, Darbee may refer to the spiritual head or leader of the Church, such as the Pope or a bishop. It may also be related to the Latin word principium - beginning or origin, as in the beginning of faith (Romans 1:17).
